slides.title: 4 label words, *decoded*
slides.sub: Some are strictly regulated. One means whatever the brand wants.

slides.title: "Hypoallergenic"
slides.body: There's *no federal standard* for it in the US. Each brand decides what it means, and doesn't have to prove it to the FDA.

slides.title: "Broad spectrum"
slides.body: SPF mostly measures UVB. Broad spectrum means it was tested to protect against *UVA too*.
slides.fix: Look for both: SPF 30+ and broad spectrum.

slides.title: "Water resistant"
slides.body: US labels can only say *40 or 80 minutes*. There's no such thing as a waterproof sunscreen.
slides.fix: Reapply after that time when you swim or sweat.

slides.title: years
slides.body: No expiration date on your sunscreen? The FDA says treat it as *expired 3 years after purchase*. Don't know when you bought it? Replace it.
